subject: Emergency unpin procedure for Private clusters — request for review
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, irene.choi@redwood.ai
Cc: Sandy Park <sandy.park@acmecloud.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Emergency unpin procedure for Private clusters — request for review

Team,

Quick summary: AcmeHealth hit a blocker with the pinned runtime (v3.4.1) — third-party dependency CVE in the image scannner requires us to unpin to v3.4.2 or apply an emergency patch. Customer is asking for an expedited unpin in their VPC deployment.

I'm proposing an "emergency unpin" procedure (attached) that is intentionally conservative and includes:
- 5% canary on a single AZ for 30 minutes
- preflight checks (schema version, KV cache compatibility, latency smoke tests)
- automated rollback trigger tied to SLO breaches (95th p95 latency > 200ms or error rate > 1%)
- clear escape hatch to reapply pin at the previous image if we detect any data or state anomalies

Please review the attached runbook (unpin-runbook-v1.2.md) and the minimal helm diff (helm-chart-diff.patch). I need sign-off from infra (Karthik), runtime (Vivek), and ops scheduling (Irene).

Questions I want resolved before we propose a window to AcmeHealth:
1) Exact preflight checklist (what to run and where).
2) Canary size and rollback thresholds.
3) Ops staffing and on-call escalation steps.
4) Any customer blackout constraints (Sandy, can you confirm).

Target: if we get sign-off today we will ask AcmeHealth for a 02:00–03:00 PT emergency window tomorrow (Wed). If they decline, we escalate the mitigation (hotpatch) path.

Attachments: unpin-runbook-v1.2.md, helm-chart-diff.patch

Thanks,

Laura Bennett
Head of Private Deployments | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, irene.choi@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Emergency unpin procedure for Private clusters — request for review

Laura — thanks for the quick writeup and the runbook. A few notes from infra/runtime perspective:

- Preflight checklist: add a KV-cache warmup and KV TTL check (we saw cache key eviction mismatches after a pin change in staging last quarter). Also include a check on token/prefix cache population to avoid steady-state cold-start errors.
- Canary: 5% across a single AZ is fine for control plane changes, but for image/runtime unpins I recommend splitting the 5% as 2x slices (2.5% -> observe 15m -> 2.5% -> observe 15m) so we can stop between slices without a full rollback.
- Rollback: include both automatic and manual rollback. Automatic rollback should be gated by an aggregated health score (error rate + p95 + memory pressure) rather than a single metric. I propose: error rate > 0.8% sustained for 10m OR p95 > 220ms sustained for 10m OR >20% increase in OOM events.
- DB migrations: confirm there are zero schema migrations in this minor release. If any DB-level changes are present, we do NOT unpin — we must follow the DB migration playbook.

I've annotated the helm-chart-diff.patch with a small toggle (runtime.imageTag) and a canaryWeight parameter. I'll attach that to the runbook as a recommended guard.

Karthik
Sr Principal, Infra | Redwood Inference

+1 on Karthik's suggestions. A couple items to add:
- Telemetry: we need a short-lived dashboard (prefilled queries) that shows request counts, 4xx/5xx split, p95/p99, and memory OOM signals for the canary hosts. This must be watchable by on-call without digging into traces.
- Auto-unpin toggle: add a manual CLI toggle (r-infra unpin abort/commit) that on-call can flip to stop further slices.
- SLA impact: if we proceed with an emergency unpin and hit a rollback, product may request credit review. Ops/sales should be aware so we can pre-authorize a discretionary credit bucket.

I can wire the dashboard with the infra team today; need 90m.

— Vivek
Head of Runtime Engineering

Laura / team — thanks for the rapid coordination. A few constraints from AcmeHealth:
- Change freeze window today until 18:00 PT; we cannot perform changes tonight.
- We can open a short emergency window tomorrow between 02:30–03:15 PT but require a 30-minute pre-change notification and a single point of contact on our side (Tim Hooper, cc'd).
- No DB schema changes allowed during emergency windows; if you detect unexpected DB migrations, stop immediately and escalate to our DB lead.

We are OK with the conservative canary approach (split slices) and the explicit rollback triggers you described. Please send the final runbook link and the pre-change notification at least 30 minutes before the start.

Sandy Park
Infrastructure Lead, AcmeHealth
Sandy.Park@acmecloud.com
